name: Combined Dystonia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Combined Dystonia

criteria.description: Presence of dystonia combined with additional neurological features such as parkinsonism or myoclonus
Exclusion of acquired or secondary causes of dystonia through clinical and laboratory evaluation
Identification of pathogenic mutations in known dystonia-associated genes (e.g., DYT1, DYT11)
Progressive or fluctuating course with involvement of multiple body regions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of dystonia with additional neurological features (major criteria) and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical evaluation remains primary.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental or generalized dystonia with combined movement disorder features
searchTerms: generalized dystonia with other movement issues

pathognomonic.symptomName: Coexisting parkinsonism characterized by bradykinesia and rigidity

common.symptomName: Cranio-cervical dystonia involving neck and facial muscles
searchTerms: involuntary contractions of neck and facial muscles

common.symptomName: Gait disturbances due to combined dystonia and parkinsonism
searchTerms: gait issues due to dystonia and parkinsonism
difficulty walking with combined movement problems

occasional.symptomName: Oculomotor abnormalities such as impaired saccades

searchTerms: problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including depression and anxiety
searchTerms: mental health issues like sadness and worry

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests excluding secondary causes
Elevated copper or ceruloplasmin levels excluded to rule out Wilson disease
imaging: Brain MRI may show basal ganglia abnormalities or be normal
Functional imaging (DAT scan) may reveal presynaptic dopaminergic deficits
genetic: Mutations in TOR1A (DYT1), SGCE (DYT11), or other dystonia-related genes
Genetic panel testing recommended for familial cases
other: Electromyography showing co-contraction of antagonist muscles
Response to levodopa or other dopaminergic agents may be variable

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated dystonia without additional neurological features
Earlier onset with no parkinsonism or myoclonus

redFlags: Rapid progression of symptoms over weeks
Presence of systemic signs suggesting secondary causes
Failure to respond to standard dystonia treatments
references: Albanese A, et al. Phenomenology and classification of dystonia: a consensus update. Mov Disord. 2013.
Marras C, et al. Combined dystonia: clinical features and treatment. Parkinsonism Relat Disord. 2016.
